//: The home page's polyfill cards (polyfills: the MCP extensions; beyond: outside MCP) and audiences. Read by PolyfillCards.vue and scripts/agents.mjs; the audiences only by the latter (the Markdown copies for agents). Every line is taken from the repository's README and each polyfill's README, in the README's order: keep them in step when those change. The recordings are Claude Code sessions, and their alt text says so.

polyfills.name: Events
polyfills.line: The agent watches events on your MCP servers, by poll, push or webhook, and an event wakes an idle session.
polyfills.alt: In Claude Code, asked to watch a Worker on Cloudflare and say what breaks, Claude starts a watch through Cloudflare's MCP server, and the session goes idle. When the Worker throws an error, the idle session wakes by itself, reads the event and says what broke: a SyntaxError in the Worker.
polyfills.addStep: Try it with the hosted demo server (no sign-in):
polyfills.ask: Give me a demo button and tell me what I type when I press it
polyfills.then: In Codex, a woken session is a Codex CLI session (the terminal app or `codex exec`). A chat in the ChatGPT desktop app keeps its events but can't be woken, so ask it for `recent_events`.

polyfills.name: Skills
polyfills.line: Skills an MCP server serves show up next to your own, load only after you say yes to each one, and are checked against the server's digests.
polyfills.alt: In Claude Code, /mcp-skills lists the skills Hugging Face's MCP server serves. Asked to use huggingface-local-models for a 16 GB Mac, Claude asks to load it and Claude Code asks once for approval; the skill and its files are read from the server, and Claude answers from it.
polyfills.addStep: Try it with Hugging Face's public MCP server (no sign-in):
polyfills.add: claude mcp add --transport http huggingface https://huggingface.co/mcp
polyfills.ask: Which GGUF quantization should I use to run a 7B model on a 16 GB Mac?
polyfills.then: In Claude Code, `/mcp-skills` lists what it serves. In Codex, the served skills appear in the `$` list from your next session.

polyfills.name: Server Cards
polyfills.line: Name a company and the agent finds the MCP servers its domain publishes, and adds the one you pick. Servers behind OAuth work.
polyfills.alt: In Claude Code, the question What MCP servers does neon.com publish? lists Neon and Neon Docs from neon.com's own catalog, each with an Add button. Add is pressed on Neon Docs, which is marked added, with a note to run /mcp to connect or sign in.
polyfills.ask: What MCP servers does neon.com publish?
polyfills.then: Then add Neon Docs (no sign-in): press Add in Claude Code, or choose "Add it" in Codex's form.

polyfills.name: Apps
polyfills.line: A server's app opens right under the tool call in the terminal, and answers the mouse and keyboard.
polyfills.alt: In Claude Code, Play DOOM opens the game from the hosted arcade server under the tool call, and it is played with clicks and keys. A system monitor app draws a live CPU chart, and in a terminal with no image support it draws the chart in text. Then a 3D torus knot renders inline and turns when dragged.
polyfills.addStep: Try it with the hosted arcade (classic shareware games from archive.org):
polyfills.ask: Find a shareware game in the arcade and load it

audiences.title: If you use Claude Code or Codex
audiences.text: Installing takes one line and trying it takes one more.

audiences.title: If you build
audiences.text: The `create-polyfill` and `design-extension` skills, and the contract every polyfill here meets. New polyfills, and existing ones brought to another host, are welcome.

audiences.title: If you write specs
audiences.text: A polyfill can be the client half of the two implementations an extension needs to reach Stable.

beyond.name: ARD discovery
beyond.spec: Agentic Resource Discovery v0.91, a draft outside MCP
beyond.line: Finds MCP servers through a domain's ard.json, or by searching an ARD registry you choose, and hands the cards to Server Cards.
beyond.alt: In Claude Code, What does buildkite.com list via ARD? shows Buildkite's MCP server with an Add button. Then a search of an ARD registry for a server that checks CI builds: Claude Code first asks whether to send the query to the registry and up to three it refers to, and after Yes the result says where the query went.
beyond.addStep: Not in the bundle. Install it by name:
beyond.addCodex: codex plugin marketplace add idosal/AgentPolyfill && codex plugin add ard-discovery@agent-polyfill
beyond.ask: What MCP servers does buildkite.com list through ARD?
beyond.then: A domain lookup sends no query to a registry. A search sends the words of your request to the registry you chose, so every search asks you first and names where it's going.
beyond.note: Installed by name, not with the others: a search sends your words to the registry you chose, so every search asks you first.
